title: review: Q5 v5: orchestrator/planner_scorecard.py + `scorecard --planner-routing` — Planner outcomes by model × decision type × band × class × architectural, non-inferiority evidence per class, economics (P7, P13, P16)
spec:
Why: no code joins Planner invocations to downstream engineering outcomes; premium_summary (planner_runs.py:843) counts launches and tokens only. The router (planner_router.py, merged) needs class_evidence and the brief (P7/P13/P16) a Planner scorecard with cold-start priors and a CLI. Three spec review rounds (T-0683, of T-0710, of T-0727) are folded in: producer named and a dependency (planner_telemetry.py, merged as T-0708), explicit min_samples source, literal criteria with correct signs, guarded telemetry import, terminal-state restriction, exclusive fix-round ownership, bare held task id. The Planner waived a fourth spec review. READ-SIDE: the scorecard stays empty in production until Wave B wires planner_runs to emit invocation rows.
What: new module orchestrator/planner_scorecard.py plus cli.py flag `scorecard --planner-routing [--json]`.
- Inputs: invocation rows via planner_telemetry.read_invocations_with_malformed(root) (rows merged by launch_id with fields launch_id, goal_id, kind, payload_keys, decision_type, model, tier, band, task_class, architectural, started_at, material, reescalation, total_tokens, usd, latency_s, outcome), bus tasks from root/tasks/*.json, spec_review and review tasks among them. Wrap `from . import planner_telemetry` in try/except ImportError so a missing module degrades to an empty card with card["error"] = "planner_telemetry unavailable". Malformed lines counted in card["malformed"].
- min_samples: explicit parameter wins; else cfg planner.routing.min_samples when int (table may be absent); else cfg promotion.min_samples; else 20.
- Ownership (every owned task id appears in exactly one invocation's set): (1) a root execute task (no constraints.fix_round_for) belongs to the invocation of the same goal with the latest started_at <= the root's created_at (none -> unowned); (2) a fix-round task (constraints.fix_round_for set) belongs to the kind == "held" invocation of the same goal whose payload_keys[0] equals its fix_round_for target and whose started_at <= the fix round's created_at, choosing the latest such invocation; when no such held invocation exists it belongs to its lineage root's owner (attribution.lineage(task)["root"]). Wave B contract: a held invocation's payload_keys[0] is the bare held task id (no colon), so compare it directly.
- Terminal roots: merged_into set, or status == "failed", or pipeline.first_green_at present. first_pass_rate, fix_round_rate and avg_fix_rounds use terminal roots only (in-flight roots excluded); downstream_accepted_rate counts all owned roots (unresolved = not accepted). Fix-round counts per root come from the root's fix-round children regardless of which invocation owns them.
- group_key(row) -> f"{model}|{decision_type}|{band}|{task_class}|{'arch' if architectural else 'plain'}".
- build(root=STATE, *, cfg=None, min_samples=None) -> {"groups": {key: metrics}, "n", "malformed", "min_samples", "read_side_only": True}; metrics per group: n, material_rate, downstream_accepted_rate, first_pass_rate (terminal roots with pipeline.lineage_fix_rounds in (0, None) and no fix-round children), fix_round_rate, avg_fix_rounds, gate_red_rate (pipeline.gate_reds > 0 over owned tasks), review_request_changes_rate (review tasks whose inputs[0] is an owned id, verdict from review_verdict or result.verdict == request_changes), spec_review_approval_rate (same for spec_review, verdict approve), replanning_rate (a later invocation of the same goal with decision_type architectural_replan), reescalation_rate (rows reescalation True), human_intervention_rate (None unless planner_telemetry.interactive_by_goal returns a row for the goal with a day after started_at; call wrapped in try/except Exception -> None), tokens_mean, usd_mean, latency_mean, terminal_roots, evidence "sufficient"|"insufficient" (n >= min_samples).
- Thresholds: CRITERIA_MAP = {"first_pass_rate": ("first_pass_delta", ">=", -0.02), "avg_fix_rounds": ("fix_rounds_delta", "<=", 0.05), "gate_success": ("gate_success_delta", ">=", -0.02)} read from promotion.CRITERIA by those keys (overridable via cfg["promotion"]); REVIEW_CHANGES_MAX_DELTA = 0.10 with "<=" is this module's own constant (promotion's review_findings_delta is NOT used); REESCALATION_MAX = 0.2; gate_success = 1 - gate_red_rate. An equal candidate/baseline pair passes every comparison.
- class_evidence(model, decision_type, band, task_class, architectural, *, root=STATE, cfg=None, min_samples=None) -> {"n", "noninferior": True|False|None, "deltas", "failed", "reescalation_rate", "baseline_model"}: baseline group = same class with model == cfg [models].planner (fallback: rows with tier fable). None when either group has n < min_samples; False when any comparison fails or reescalation_rate > REESCALATION_MAX (failed lists "reescalation"); True otherwise. Tokens, usd, latency never enter the verdict.
- economics(root=STATE) -> per model {"planner_usd_per_accepted_goal", "planner_tokens_per_accepted_goal", "pipeline_usd_after_planning" (mean over invocations of the sum of scorecard.by_task usd for owned tasks), "expected_total_cost_after_planning": {decision_type: mean(planner usd + pipeline usd)}}; accepted goals via scorecard.accepted_goals(root).
- format(card) -> text table sorted by key with a first line 'read-side only: rows appear once planner_runs emits invocations' when n == 0; format_evidence(evidence) one line. cli.py: `sc.add_argument("--planner-routing", action="store_true")`, dispatch to build/format (json with --json), ap.error when combined with --planner or --parallelism.
acceptance: tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_groups_by_model_type_band_class_arch — rows written with planner_telemetry.record_launch/record_usage/record_materiality under a sandbox root for two models and two decision types produce four group keys with n, material_rate and downstream_accepted_rate from owned tasks

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_ownership_is_exclusive_terminal_roots_and_fix_rounds — root T1 created after invocation A belongs to A; its fix round T2 created after held invocation B with payload_keys [T1] belongs to B and not A; a fix round with no matching held invocation belongs to its root's owner; no task id appears in two owned sets; an in-flight root (no merged_into, not failed, no first_green_at) is excluded from first_pass_rate and fix_round_rate but counted as not accepted

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_class_evidence_noninferior_equivalent_worse_and_insufficient — opus identical to fable (all deltas 0) gives noninferior True with failed empty; first_pass_rate 0.3 lower gives False naming first_pass_rate; review_request_changes_rate 0.3 higher gives False naming review_request_changes_rate; n below min_samples gives None; a group with 1e9 tokens and 0 usd changes no verdict
tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_reescalation_penalises_class — reescalation_rate 0.5 on an otherwise equal class gives noninferior False with failed containing reescalation

tests/test_planner_scorecard.py::test_cli_flag_min_samples_source_and_malformed_tolerance — `scorecard --planner-routing --json` under a sandbox root prints a card with read_side_only True, groups and malformed 1 for a runs dir containing one malformed line; min_samples comes from [planner.routing] when present, else [promotion], else 20; a patched ImportError for planner_telemetry yields card error text instead of a crash

result.summary: Diff matches the spec and all five acceptance tests are present with substantive assertions: group_key format, ownership exclusivity (root/held/fix-round/lineage-fallback), terminal-root gating of first_pass/fix_round rates, class_evidence noninferiority logic (criteria from promotion.CRITERIA, module-local REVIEW_CHANGES_MAX_DELTA, reescalation gate, tokens/usd/latency excluded from verdict), and the CLI flag with correct min_samples precedence (explicit > planner.routing > promotion > 20) and ImportError fallback to an error card. _lineage_root reimplements attribution.lineage's walk locally instead of calling it directly, but that's necessary to respect the passed root parameter (attribution.lineage uses bus.get against the default root) rather than a defect. No security concerns: read-only module, no new deps, no secrets, errors fail closed to an empty/error card.
